The graph of the linear function $g$ is shown, where $y = g(x)$. What is the $y$-intercept of the graph of $g$?
explanation: Choice D is correct. The $y$-intercept of a graph is the point where the graph intersects the $y$-axis, which occurs when $x = 0$. The graph of the linear function $g$ intersects the $y$-axis at the point $(0, 3)$. Therefore, the $y$-intercept of the graph of $g$ is $(0, 3)$.
